name: Norma Cappagli
milestone_by_age_26: Won Miss World 1960 in London at age 21, becoming the first Argentine to claim the title.
early_history_summary: Born in Buenos Aires, Cappagli studied accounting before being discovered at a hair salon by the wife of French designer Jean Cartier, who offered her a modeling opportunity. She won Miss Sweater Argentina and then Miss Argentina World in October 1960 before capturing the Miss World crown in November 1960 at the Lyceum Ballroom in London.
family_context_summary: Raised by her father and aunts in Buenos Aires after family difficulties; studied accounting before entering modeling. Her brother Aldo later served as her manager.
primary_early_advantage_tags: beauty pageant pipeline, sibling manager, physical appearance, salon discovery
evidence_summary: Cappagli was studying accounting in Buenos Aires when she was discovered at a hair salon by the wife of designer Jean Cartier, which led to modeling and then the Miss World pageant pipeline. She won Miss Argentina and then Miss World 1960 at age 21 with no documented family background in fashion or entertainment. Her brother Aldo managed her career afterward. The pageant platform itself served as her primary distribution and network advantage.
starting_point: Born in Buenos Aires, Argentina to a modest family; raised by her father and aunts, studied accounting before entering modeling.
current_position: Died in December 2020 at age 81 after being struck by a bus in Buenos Aires; final role: former model and advertising professional.

trajectory.event: Won Miss World 1960 in London, becoming the first Argentine to claim the title.
Recorded the song 'Sexy World' and starred in the film 'Sexy', declining further acting offers.
Worked as an exclusive model for Christian Dior and Valentino before marrying an Italian businessman and moving to Milan.
Returned to Argentina after living in Milan and Rio de Janeiro.
Died on December 22 after being struck by a bus in Buenos Aires.

name: Pernilla Wiberg
milestone_by_age_26: Won giant slalom gold at the 1991 FIS Alpine World Championships in Saalbach at age 20, the first Scandinavian woman to win a World Championship gold in 33 years.
early_history_summary: Born in Norrköping, Sweden, Wiberg started skiing around age 10-11 at the local Yxbacken hill. She moved to the ski gymnasium in Malung at age 16 to pursue alpine racing seriously. After competing in junior world championships in 1987 and 1988 without much success, she made her World Cup debut in March 1990 and achieved her international breakthrough in the 1991 season with three World Cup victories and a World Championship gold.
family_context_summary: Born into an athletic family in Norrköping; her father was a runner and the family was sports-oriented. She was the middle child and showed strong willpower from a young age, moving away from home at 16 to attend the ski gymnasium in Malung.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was athletic (a runner) and the family was sports-oriented, though not specifically in alpine skiing. Her younger brother Andreas became a Swedish triathlon champion.
primary_early_advantage_tags: ski gymnasium Malung, Swedish national team, athletic family, early specialization, limited training conditions
evidence_summary: Wiberg grew up in Norrköping with limited local ski training conditions, but her sports-oriented family supported her move to the ski gymnasium in Malung at age 16. She described herself as 'never a super talent, a training product,' relying on intense training and willpower rather than natural gifts. The Swedish alpine skiing pipeline, including Norrköpings SK club and the national team system, provided the institutional structure for her development. Her father's athletic background and her brother's triathlon success indicate a family athletic culture.
starting_point: Born in Norrköping, Sweden to an athletic family; father was a runner, started skiing around age 10-11 at the local Yxbacken hill.
current_position: Runs Pernilla Wiberg Hotel at Idre Fjäll; works as alpine skiing commentator for SVT; lives in Monaco.

trajectory.event: Made World Cup debut in Vemdalen, finishing 5th in slalom and 3rd in giant slalom.
Won giant slalom gold at the World Championships in Saalbach, the first Scandinavian woman to win in 33 years.
Won Olympic gold in giant slalom at Albertville.
Won Olympic gold in the combined event at Lillehammer.
Won the overall World Cup title plus slalom and combined titles in a record-breaking season.
Won combined gold at the World Championships in Vail.
Retired from competitive skiing after 12 years on the World Cup circuit with 24 race victories.
Opened Pernilla Wiberg Hotel at Idre Fjäll and began working as SVT alpine skiing commentator.

name: Hana Mašková
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship bronze in 1967 at age 17, followed by European gold and Olympic bronze in 1968 at age 18.
early_history_summary: Born in Prague, Mašková started skating at age 5 at the Štvanice Stadium, where coach Karel Glogar identified her talent. She competed in her first competition at age 8 and won her first title at 10. She made her international debut at the 1963 European Championships at age 13, and by 17 had won World and European medals. Her mother was a constant presence rinkside and was described as a stage mother.
family_context_summary: Father Joseph Mašek was a hotel waiter and mother Marie Mašková was a cook at a kindergarten. Her mother had suffered tragedy in a previous marriage (first husband murdered two of her children) and was a demanding stage mother who was always rinkside during training.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not in the skating domain; father was a hotel waiter and mother a kindergarten cook. No family connection to figure skating is documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Štvanice Stadium, Karel Glogar, multiple coaches, early start age 5, stage mother, Czechoslovak skating system
evidence_summary: Mašková started skating at age 5 at Prague's Štvanice Stadium, where coach Karel Glogar (who had previously worked with two-time World champion Ája Vrzáňová) identified her talent. She received sustained coaching from multiple dedicated coaches (Glogar, Sadílek, Nováková, Koudelka) and trained intensively, getting up at 4am daily before school. Her working-class parents were not in the skating domain, but her mother was a demanding stage mother. The Czechoslovak figure skating system provided the institutional pipeline, and Prague's Štvanice Stadium provided early access to ice facilities.
starting_point: Born in Prague, Czechoslovakia to a hotel waiter father and kindergarten cook mother; started skating at age 5 at the Štvanice Stadium.
current_position: Died in March 1972 at age 22 in a car crash near Vouvray, France; final role: professional figure skater with Holiday on Ice.

trajectory.event: Made international debut at the European Championships in Budapest, finishing 15th.
Won silver at European Championships in Ljubljana and bronze at World Championships in Vienna.
Won European gold in Västerås and Olympic bronze at the Grenoble Winter Olympics.
Won European silver in Garmisch-Partenkirchen and retired from competition to join Holiday on Ice.
Killed in a car crash near Vouvray, France on March 31.

name: Romuald Klim
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Klim started hammer throw training around 1955 at age 22 and was virtually unknown until the 1963 season at age 30. His Olympic gold came in 1964 at age 31.
early_history_summary: Born in a farmer's family in Khvoevo, Belarus, Klim entered the Belarusian State Institute of Physical Education and began hammer throwing around 1955 at age 22. He worked as a physical education teacher at the Gorki Agricultural Academy and was not noticed by Soviet sports officials until 1963.
family_context_summary: Born in a farmer's family in the village of Khvoevo, Nesvizh District, Belarus.
evidence_summary: Klim was born into a farming family in Belarus and entered the Belarusian State Institute of Physical Education, where he initially did discus throwing before switching to hammer throw around 1955 at age 22. He was virtually unknown before the 1963 season at age 30, when he won the Riga Cup and finished second at the Soviet Championships. His Olympic gold medal came in 1964 at age 31, well beyond the age-26 threshold.

name: Luis de Pablo
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. De Pablo studied law and worked as a legal advisor at Iberia Airlines through his early twenties. His first public musical activities (founding Grupo Nueva Música, organizing Tiempo y Música concerts) came in 1958-1959 at ages 28-29.
early_history_summary: Born in Bilbao, Spain, de Pablo lost his father in the Spanish Civil War and moved to Madrid at age 6. He started composing at 12 but studied law at the Complutense University, graduating in 1952. He worked briefly as a legal advisor at Iberia Airlines before pursuing music full-time in the late 1950s.
family_context_summary: Born in Bilbao; lost his father in the Spanish Civil War and moved to Madrid with his mother and siblings at age 6. Family circumstances made an artistic career impossible initially, leading him to study law.
evidence_summary: De Pablo started composing at age 12 but the Spanish Civil War's impact on his family (losing his father) forced him to study law instead of music. He graduated in 1952 at age 22 and worked as a legal advisor at Iberia Airlines while studying music independently. His first public musical activities came in 1958 (founding Grupo Nueva Música at age 28) and 1959 (organizing Tiempo y Música concerts at age 29). No material, independently verifiable milestone occurred by age 26.

name: Sylvester Stallone
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Stallone appeared in a soft-core adult film (1970) and small uncredited roles in Klute (1971) and Bananas (1971) before age 26, but his breakthrough came with The Lords of Flatbush (1974) at age 28 and Rocky (1976) at age 30.
early_history_summary: Born in Hell's Kitchen, Manhattan, Stallone had a difficult childhood in foster care and a broken home. He attended the American College in Switzerland on an athletic scholarship, then studied drama at the University of Miami before leaving for New York City in 1969 to pursue acting. He struggled for years with minor roles and odd jobs before his breakthrough.
family_context_summary: Born to Jacqueline Stallone (celebrity astrologer and women's wrestling promoter) and Francesco Stallone Sr. (hairdresser and Italian immigrant). Parents divorced in 1957; Stallone spent time in foster care and attended multiple schools, being expelled from several.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was an astrologer and wrestling promoter; father was a hairdresser and Italian immigrant. Neither parent was in the film industry, though his mother's show business connections may have provided some exposure.
evidence_summary: Stallone struggled as an actor throughout his early twenties, appearing in a soft-core adult film (The Party at Kitty and Stud's, 1970) and small uncredited roles in Klute (1971) and Bananas (1971). By age 26 (July 1972), he had no material milestone in film. His first significant role came with The Lords of Flatbush (1974) at age 28, and his career-defining breakthrough was Rocky (1976) at age 30, which he wrote and starred in.

name: Phil Esposito
milestone_by_age_26: Became an NHL regular with the Chicago Black Hawks in the 1964-65 season at age 22, scoring 23 goals and 55 points in 70 games while centering for Bobby Hull.
early_history_summary: Born in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, Esposito grew up playing hockey on frozen ponds and outdoor rinks with his brother Tony. He signed with the Chicago Black Hawks as a teenager and was assigned to junior and minor league teams. After a sparkling junior season with the St. Catharines Teepees in 1961-62 and two minor league seasons with the St. Louis Braves, he was called up to the NHL midway through the 1963-64 season and became a regular the following year.
family_context_summary: Born to Pat and Frances Esposito, both of Italian descent, in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario. His father quit school as a teenager to work in steel mills, later working as a labourer and welder, and built the family's first house for $3,000. Brother Tony also became an NHL player and Hockey Hall of Famer.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not in the hockey domain; father was a steel mill worker and welder. However, the family's immersion in Canadian hockey culture and the brothers' shared development was significant.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chicago Black Hawks signing, Canadian hockey heartland, brother Tony, outdoor rinks, junior hockey pipeline, Italian immigrant working-class background
evidence_summary: Esposito grew up in a working-class Italian-Canadian family in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, a hockey heartland with abundant outdoor rinks. He and his brother Tony (also a future NHL Hall of Famer) started playing hockey together from an early age. The Chicago Black Hawks organization signed him as a teenager and developed him through junior (St. Catharines Teepees) and minor league (St. Louis Braves) pipelines before his NHL call-up. His father's steel mill labor background meant no financial platform, but the Canadian hockey ecosystem and sibling rivalry provided strong developmental advantages.
starting_point: Born in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario to an Italian-Canadian working-class family; father was a steel mill worker and welder who built the family home for $3,000.
current_position: Hockey Hall of Famer and current broadcaster for the Tampa Bay Lightning; resides in the Tampa Bay area.

trajectory.event: Made NHL debut with the Chicago Black Hawks midway through the 1963-64 season.
Established as an NHL regular, centering for Bobby Hull and scoring 55 points in 70 games.
Traded to the Boston Bruins in a blockbuster deal that transformed his career.
Became first NHL player to score 100+ points in a season with 126 points, winning the Art Ross and Hart trophies.
Won first of two consecutive Stanley Cups with the Boston Bruins.
Set NHL records with 76 goals and 152 points in a single season.
Inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame.
Founded the Tampa Bay Lightning as general manager and head coach.

name: Alena Šeredová
milestone_by_age_26: Won first runner-up at Miss Czech Republic 1998 at age 20 and placed 4th at Miss World 1998, the best result by a Czech woman at the time.
early_history_summary: Born in Prague, Šeredová began modeling at age 14, working with top Czech fashion photographer Jadran Šetlík by 15. By 17 she had arrived in Milan, the Italian fashion capital. In 1998 at age 20, she won first runner-up at Miss Czech Republic and represented her country at Miss World 1998, placing 4th.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical appearance and early modeling exposure
family_context_summary: Born in Prague's Vinohrady district to parents who supported her early modeling career. She has a younger sister Eliška. Family financial background is not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No family connections to modeling or fashion are mentioned.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Miss Czech Republic pageant, photographer Jadran Šetlík, early modeling start, Milan fashion capital, physical appearance
evidence_summary: Šeredová started modeling at 14 and was photographed by top Czech fashion photographer Jadran Šetlík by age 15, providing early professional exposure. By 17, she had traveled to Milan, a European fashion capital, giving her geographic proximity to the modeling industry. The Miss Czech Republic and Miss World pageant pipeline in 1998 provided her primary platform at age 20. No family background in fashion or modeling is documented, and her physical appearance was the primary driver of her early opportunities.
starting_point: Born in Prague's Vinohrady district, Czechoslovakia; started modeling at age 14 with Czech fashion photographer Jadran Šetlík.
current_position: Model, actress, and TV personality living in Italy; married Italian businessman Alessandro Nasi in 2023; formerly married to goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon.

Chosen to pose for the Max Calendar, cementing her status as a top model in Italy.

Married Italian businessman Alessandro Nasi.

name: Sean Kelly
milestone_by_age_26: Won first professional races in 1978 at age 22, including the Tour de Romandie and Grand Prix d'Isbergues, after turning professional with Flandria in 1977.
early_history_summary: Born into a farming family in Curraghduff, County Waterford, Ireland, Kelly left school at 13 to work on the farm after his father was hospitalized. He became a bricklayer at 16. He started cycling with the Carrick Wheelers club in 1970, won his first race at 14, and dominated Irish junior and senior amateur racing as a teenager. After being barred from the 1976 Olympics for riding in South Africa, he moved to France as an amateur and was recruited by Belgian team Flandria in 1977.
family_context_summary: Second son of Jack (John) and Nellie Kelly, a farming family on a 45-48 acre smallholding in Curraghduff, County Waterford. Left school at 13 to help on the farm after his father was hospitalized with an ulcer; became a bricklayer at 16. Grew up in modest rural circumstances.
parent_family_domain_summary: Farming family with no connection to cycling. His older brother Joe started cycling to school and joined the Carrick Wheelers club, which Sean followed into.
primary_early_advantage_tags: farming poverty, left school at 13, Carrick Wheelers, brother Joe, Olympic ban, Jean de Gribaldy, rural Ireland, precocious talent
evidence_summary: Kelly grew up in poverty on a small Irish farm, leaving school at 13 to work after his father's hospitalization and becoming a bricklayer at 16. He found cycling through his brother Joe and the Carrick Wheelers club, showing precocious talent by winning his first race at 14. Being barred from the 1976 Olympics for riding in South Africa under a false name forced him to turn professional, a pivotal adversity that shaped his career. Belgian manager Jean de Gribaldy traveled to the family farm to recruit him. His rural Irish upbringing provided no financial platform but created intense drive and physical toughness.
starting_point: Born into a farming family in Curraghduff, County Waterford, Ireland; left school at 13 to work on the farm, became a bricklayer at 16.
current_position: Former professional cyclist with 193 career wins; works as cycling commentator for Eurosport; involved in Sean Kelly Cycling Academy in Belgium.

trajectory.event: Won the Shay Elliott Memorial Race as a senior competitor while still junior-eligible.
Turned professional with Belgian team Flandria after Jean de Gribaldy recruited him at his family farm.
Won first professional races including the Tour de Romandie and Grand Prix d'Isbergues.
Won Paris-Nice for the first of seven consecutive years, establishing himself as a top Classics rider.
Won Paris-Roubaix and Liège-Bastogne-Liège, two Monument classics.
Won the Vuelta a España, his only Grand Tour overall victory.
Won the inaugural UCI Road World Cup.
Retired from professional cycling with 193 career victories.

name: Ela Bhatt
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Bhatt earned her law degree in 1954 at age 21 and joined the Textile Labour Association's legal department in 1955 at age 22, but her founding of SEWA came in 1972 at age 39.
early_history_summary: Born in Ahmedabad, India, Bhatt earned a BA in English in 1952 and a law degree in 1954 with a gold medal for Hindu law. She joined the Textile Labour Association's legal department in 1955 and taught English briefly at SNDT Women's University. She was asked to head the TLA's women's wing in 1968 at age 35, which led to her founding SEWA in 1972.
family_context_summary: Born in Ahmedabad to Sumantrai Bhatt, a successful lawyer, and Vanalila Vyas, who was active in the women's movement and served as secretary of the All India Women's Conference. Middle child of three sisters, childhood spent in Surat.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a successful lawyer and mother was active in the women's movement, providing both legal and social activism domain exposure from an early age.
evidence_summary: Bhatt came from a privileged background with a lawyer father and a mother active in the women's movement. She earned her law degree in 1954 at age 21 and joined the Textile Labour Association's legal department in 1955. However, her career-defining achievement—founding the Self-Employed Women's Association (SEWA)—came in 1972 at age 39, well beyond the age-26 threshold. By age 26, she was working as a lawyer at TLA, which does not constitute a material, independently verifiable milestone.

name: Helmuth Koinigg
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Formula Super Vee championship in 1973 at age 24 and entered Formula One in 1974 at age 25, racing for Martini Porsche at Le Mans and making two F1 Grand Prix starts with Surtees.
early_history_summary: Born in Vienna, Koinigg grew up in the Styrian mountains and was a member of the Austrian national junior B skiing team before turning to motorsport. He began racing with a Mini Cooper purchased from Niki Lauda in 1969, progressing through touring cars, Formula Vee, and Formula Ford. Helmut Marko invited him to test a Formula Vee car, leading to a drive with the McNamara team and then Kurt Bergmann's Kaimann team, where he won the 1973 Formula Super Vee title.
family_context_summary: Came from a comfortable background in Vienna. He studied engineering and journalism and lived in Sweden for several months in 1966. Despite the comfortable family background, raising money to go racing proved to be a problem throughout his career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No family connections to motorsport are mentioned, though the comfortable background may have facilitated early racing activities.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Niki Lauda connection, Helmut Marko mentor, Martini Porsche, Kaimann team, Austrian motorsport, skiing background, comfortable family
evidence_summary: Koinigg came from a comfortable Vienna background and had athletic ability as a junior national skier before turning to motorsport. His purchase of a Mini Cooper from Niki Lauda and subsequent discovery by Helmut Marko, who invited him to test a Formula Vee car, were pivotal network connections in the Austrian racing community. He progressed through Formula Vee with the Kaimann team, winning the 1973 European title, then moved to sports car racing with Martini Porsche and F1 with Surtees in 1974. Despite his comfortable background, he had to raise money to buy racing seats, indicating financial constraints relative to the costs of motorsport.
starting_point: Born in Vienna, Austria to a comfortable family; grew up in the Styrian mountains and was a junior national skier before turning to motorsport.
current_position: Died in October 1974 at age 25 in a crash at the United States Grand Prix at Watkins Glen; final role: Formula One driver for Surtees.

trajectory.event: Began racing career with a Mini Cooper purchased from Niki Lauda, competing in touring car races.
Finished third in the European Formula Super Vee championship driving for Kurt Bergmann's Kaimann team.
Won the European Formula Super Vee championship title.
Raced for Martini Porsche at Le Mans and made Formula One debut with Surtees, finishing 10th in Canada.
Killed on October 6 in a crash at the United States Grand Prix at Watkins Glen due to barrier failure.

name: Domagoj Duvnjak
milestone_by_age_26: Made senior debut in the Croatian first division at age 16 in 2004, became the league's top scorer before 18, and won silver at the 2008 European Championship with Croatia at age 20.
early_history_summary: Born in Đakovo, Croatia into a handball family, Duvnjak started accompanying his father (a handball coach) to practice at age 5 and began playing at 9. He made his senior debut for RK Đakovo in the Croatian first division at age 14-16 and became the league's top scorer before 18. In 2006, coach Lino Cervar brought him to RK Zagreb, where he won three consecutive league and cup titles and made his Croatian national team debut.
family_context_summary: Born into a handball family in Đakovo, Croatia. His father was a handball coach at RK Đakovo (and former player at Medveščak), his mother played handball, his sister played handball, his uncle was a player and coach, and his cousins all played. The entire family was immersed in the sport.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a handball coach and former player at Medveščak, mother played handball, uncle was a player and coach, and sister and cousins all played. The family provided direct domain expertise and coaching from the earliest age.
primary_early_advantage_tags: handball family, father coach, RK Đakovo first division, Lino Cervar mentor, Croatian national team, early senior debut age 16, total family immersion
evidence_summary: Duvnjak was born into an extraordinary handball family where his father coached, his mother played, his sister played, his uncle coached, and his cousins all played. He started attending practices with his father at age 5 and playing at 9, making his senior debut in the Croatian first division at 14-16 and becoming the league's top scorer before 18. Coach Lino Cervar recognized his talent and brought him to RK Zagreb at 18, where he won three consecutive league and cup titles. The family-domain apprenticeship was exceptionally strong, with direct and sustained coaching from his father and uncle from the earliest age.
starting_point: Born in Đakovo, Croatia into a handball family; father was a handball coach at RK Đakovo, mother and sister were handball players.
current_position: Captain of THW Kiel and one of the greatest handball players of all time; IHF World Player of the Year 2013; retired from Croatian national team in 2025 as its all-time appearance and goal leader.

trajectory.event: Made senior debut for RK Đakovo in the Croatian first division.
Transferred to RK Zagreb and made debut for the Croatian national team.
Won silver medal at the EHF European Championship with Croatia.
Signed with HSV Hamburg for a record transfer fee, becoming the most expensive handball player in history.
Won the EHF Champions League with Hamburg and was named IHF World Player of the Year.
Joined THW Kiel, where he would become captain and win multiple Bundesliga titles.
Won the EHF Champions League with THW Kiel.
Retired from the Croatian national team as its all-time appearance and goal leader.
